concept.name: Node
concept.definition: A node is any computer running blockchain client software that connects to peers, propagates transactions and blocks, and verifies data against the protocol's consensus rules.
concept.intuition: Every node keeps its own copy of the ledger and checks the math itself — 'don't trust, verify'.
concept.mechanics: Full nodes download and validate every block and re-execute transactions, pruning old state; archive nodes additionally retain all historical states; light nodes download only block headers and request proofs from full nodes. On Ethereum a node pairs an execution client (EVM/state) with a consensus client (proof-of-stake).
concept.failure_modes: If most users rely on a few hosted node/RPC providers, the network re-centralizes in practice even with many independent nodes; a bug in a dominant client can take down a large share of the network simultaneously.
concept.misconceptions: Running a node does not by itself earn rewards — only miners (PoW) or validators (PoS) are paid. A light node trusts block headers and does not fully verify state.
concept.example: An Ethereum full node stores recent state (typically the last 128 blocks), verifies every new block against consensus rules, and serves data to light clients and wallets via its RPC endpoint.

citations.source: Ethereum.org developer docs - Nodes and clients
